title: Securing Global Retail API Endpoints
business: E-commerce retailers managing public-facing APIs for mobile applications and web storefronts.
problem: Unprotected web endpoints are susceptible to common exploits like SQL injection and cross-site scripting, which can lead to unauthorized data access and service disruption.
solution: Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) provides centralized protection for web applications by inspecting incoming traffic against managed and custom rules to block malicious requests before they reach the backend.
steps: Deploy an Azure Application Gateway or Front Door instance to serve as the entry point for web traffic.
Enable the WAF policy and associate it with the application delivery service.
Configure managed rule sets to provide baseline protection against common web vulnerabilities.
Define custom rules to address specific application logic or block traffic from known malicious IP ranges.
Monitor WAF logs in Azure Monitor to analyze blocked requests and refine rule sensitivity.
outcome: Enhanced security posture with reduced exposure to common web-based attacks and improved visibility into malicious traffic patterns.
limitation: Strict rule configurations can lead to false positives where legitimate user traffic is blocked; this requires ongoing tuning and testing in detection mode before enforcing block actions.
